candidates.name: The Hague
candidates.summary: International seat of government with tram-served neighborhoods, North Sea beaches, major museums and a calmer daily rhythm than Amsterdam.

candidates.name: San Ramón
candidates.summary: Cooler coffee-country town with a walkable center, regional hospital and authentic Costa Rican daily life, balanced by rain, Spanish dependence and limited urban amenities.

candidates.name: St. John's
candidates.summary: Colourful Atlantic capital with serious coastal hiking, universities, healthcare and nightlife, offset by wind, fog, winter weather and geographic isolation.

candidates.name: Santa Fe
candidates.summary: Adobe state capital with an outsized art, food and museum scene, immediate mountain access and significant housing, altitude and healthcare tradeoffs.

candidates.name: St. Cloud
candidates.summary: Central Minnesota service hub on the Mississippi with attainable housing, strong healthcare, colleges and excellent regional trails—but severe winters and car dependence.

candidates.name: Kyoto
candidates.summary: Japan’s former imperial capital: temple districts, university neighborhoods, exceptional rail access and intense seasonal tourism inside a hot-summer basin.

candidates.name: Ajijic
candidates.summary: A colorful Lake Chapala village known for cobblestone streets, a lively arts community, mild highland weather, and one of Mexico's most established international-resident networks. Guadalajara broadens airport and specialist-care access.

candidates.name: Boquete
candidates.summary: A green highland town surrounded by coffee farms, cloud-forest trails, and mountain scenery, with a cooler climate and an established international community. David supplies broader shopping and specialist services.

candidates.name: Chiang Mai
candidates.summary: Northern Thailand's cultural capital offers temples, markets, mountain access, healthcare, cafés, and creative energy—alongside a serious seasonal smoke problem. Neighborhood choice and season matter enormously here.

candidates.name: Cuenca
candidates.summary: A cultured Andean city of rivers, plazas, markets, and historic architecture, offering an urban lifestyle at high elevation with a well-established international community. The tram and river corridors shape everyday movement.

candidates.name: Da Nang
candidates.summary: A fast-growing Vietnamese coastal city with a broad urban beach, riverfront districts, excellent regional access, abundant food, and a modern everyday pace. Its airport makes regional travel unusually convenient.

candidates.name: Florianópolis
candidates.summary: An island-and-mainland city celebrated for beaches, trails, lagoons, surfing, and technology, with neighborhood lifestyles ranging from urban to distinctly coastal. Island traffic makes neighborhood choice especially important.

candidates.name: Funchal
candidates.summary: Madeira's subtropical capital rises from the Atlantic in steep, garden-filled neighborhoods, offering urban services, dramatic scenery, and year-round outdoor access. Steep slopes make address selection unusually consequential.

candidates.name: George Town
candidates.summary: Penang's heritage capital combines celebrated street food, multicultural neighborhoods, historic architecture, modern hospitals, and island access in a hot tropical setting. The wider Penang urban area extends well beyond the old town.

candidates.name: Hua Hin
candidates.summary: A long-established Thai beach city known for golf, markets, hospitals, seafood, and relatively easy access to Bangkok, with a relaxed but seasonal rhythm. Central and outlying districts function very differently.

candidates.name: Lucca
candidates.summary: A refined Tuscan city enclosed by Renaissance walls, with a walkable center, cycling, music, markets, and rail access to Pisa and Florence. Life inside and outside the walls feels meaningfully different.

candidates.name: Mérida
candidates.summary: Yucatán's gracious capital blends Maya heritage, colonial architecture, neighborhood markets, strong regional healthcare, and an active cultural calendar with serious tropical heat. Its neighborhoods offer sharply different versions of city life.

candidates.name: Monopoli
candidates.summary: A working Adriatic port city in Puglia where a whitewashed old town, small beaches, seafood, and rail links support an appealing coastal routine. Its winter rhythm is quieter and more locally focused.

candidates.name: Montevideo
candidates.summary: Uruguay's relaxed coastal capital pairs long Rambla walks, distinctive neighborhoods, cultural life, and strong urban services with a comparatively high regional cost of living. Each major neighborhood has a notably different personality.

candidates.name: Nafplio
candidates.summary: A picturesque Peloponnese seafront city with a walkable old town, fortress views, café-lined squares, and easy access to major archaeological sites. Its quieter off-season character deserves equal attention.

candidates.name: Nice
candidates.summary: A sophisticated Mediterranean city with beaches, markets, museums, tram service, a major airport, and effortless access to the French Riviera and nearby Italy. Neighborhood selection can reduce both cost and crowding.

candidates.name: Palm Springs
candidates.summary: A design-forward desert city known for mid-century architecture, mountain views, golf, LGBTQ+ community life, and winter sunshine—balanced by extreme summer heat. Seasonal population changes are part of its identity.

candidates.name: Paphos
candidates.summary: A sunny Cypriot coastal city combining archaeological sites, beaches, an international community, and its own airport with a spread-out, car-oriented layout. Coastal, central, and hillside communities function quite differently.

candidates.name: Santander
candidates.summary: A green northern Spanish bay city with beaches, promenades, cultural institutions, healthcare, and a cooler Atlantic climate than the Mediterranean coast. Its Atlantic weather creates a distinctly greener lifestyle.

candidates.name: Savannah
candidates.summary: A deeply atmospheric Southern city of live-oak squares, historic architecture, art, food, and riverfront energy, with heat, humidity, storms, and tourism to consider. Block-level conditions matter more than the postcard image suggests.

candidates.name: Šibenik
candidates.summary: A compact Adriatic city of stone lanes, fortresses, waterfront life, and island access, positioned between the coast and Krka National Park. The difference between summer and winter is substantial.

candidates.name: Begur
candidates.summary: Life in Begur is shaped by a choice: the hilltop village or the coves below it.

candidates.name: Calpe / Calp
candidates.summary: In Calpe, the sea can fit into an ordinary weekday.

candidates.name: Syros
candidates.summary: On Syros, a long stay can begin with the routines of a small city rather than a beach resort.

candidates.name: Voula
candidates.summary: Voula makes coastal living feel like a neighbourhood routine.

candidates.name: Akyaka
candidates.summary: Akyaka’s appeal is in the short distance between very different settings: the small coastal centre, the Azmak River and the pine-covered slopes above the Gulf of Gökova.

candidates.name: Calella de Palafrugell
candidates.summary: Calella de Palafrugell is a place where a short walk can be the point of the day.

candidates.name: Altea
candidates.summary: In Altea, the day can begin on the level seafront and end above the rooftops, beside the blue domes of Nuestra Señora del Consuelo.

candidates.name: Jávea / Xàbia
candidates.summary: Jávea, or Xàbia, offers three different versions of a coastal day.

candidates.name: Glyfada
candidates.summary: Glyfada gives daily life on the Athens Riviera an urban rhythm.

candidates.name: Datça
candidates.summary: Datça’s harbour gives a long stay a simple daily centre: somewhere to walk, find a meal and return to after the practical business of shopping.

candidates.name: Kaş
candidates.summary: In Kaş, the harbour and the lanes of Uzun Çarşı make a compact centre feel full of possibilities.

candidates.name: Palamós
candidates.summary: In Palamós, the harbour gives the day a purpose beyond the beach.

candidates.name: Tossa de Mar
candidates.summary: Tossa de Mar is at its most convincing when you imagine an ordinary day beneath the walls rather than a single photograph of them.

candidates.name: Villajoyosa
candidates.summary: Villajoyosa makes it easy to picture a day built around small pleasures: shopping at the Mercat, walking down to the coloured houses above the beach, and leaving time for a coffee or something cold before heading home.

candidates.name: Palaio Faliro
candidates.summary: Palaio Faliro offers a coastal version of Athens life: an apartment on a lived-in street, a pastry stop on the way out, and the waterfront close enough to become a regular habit.

candidates.name: Rhodes Town
candidates.summary: Rhodes Town lets a harbour walk, a medieval lane and an ordinary shopping trip belong to the same day.

candidates.name: Castellammare del Golfo
candidates.summary: In Castellammare del Golfo, the harbor gives an ordinary walk a destination.

candidates.name: Pizzo
candidates.summary: Pizzo’s appeal comes into focus around Piazza della Repubblica: a gelato, the stone presence of Castello Murat and the sea beyond the rooftops.

candidates.name: Otranto
candidates.summary: Otranto makes the sea part of a walk through town rather than a separate excursion.

candidates.name: Gallipoli
candidates.summary: In Gallipoli, crossing the bridge changes the scale of the day.

candidates.name: Bosa
candidates.summary: Bosa gives you two landscapes to live with: the Temo winding through town and the sea farther downstream.

candidates.name: Logroño
candidates.summary: In Logroño, an ordinary evening can begin with a walk past the Espolón and end with a pincho on Calle Laurel.

candidates.name: Turku
candidates.summary: The Aura River gives Turku a natural place to begin the day.

candidates.name: Mar del Plata
candidates.summary: Mar del Plata is more interesting as a place to live when the beach is allowed to be part of the day rather than the whole plan.

candidates.name: Oita
candidates.summary: Ōita’s appeal is easiest to see in an ordinary day: walking out from the station area, finding lunch in the central streets, and making time for an exhibition at OPAM before heading home.

candidates.name: Duluth
candidates.summary: Lake Superior is difficult to separate from the idea of living in Duluth.

candidates.name: Olomouc
candidates.summary: A walk across Olomouc’s old squares can turn a routine errand into the most enjoyable part of the day.

candidates.name: Maringá
candidates.summary: Maringá makes most sense as a place to build a routine: shopping, stopping for something to eat and finding a green stretch of the city to return to between appointments.

candidates.name: Yokohama
candidates.summary: Yokohama lets a waterfront walk sit comfortably alongside an ordinary working week.

candidates.name: Iowa City
candidates.summary: In Iowa City, a bookstore visit, a film and a meal downtown can form an ordinary evening rather than a special itinerary.

candidates.name: Kingston
candidates.summary: Kingston’s waterfront gives an ordinary day somewhere to go.

candidates.name: Singapore
candidates.summary: Breakfast can be the best introduction to Singapore: coffee at a neighborhood stall, something freshly cooked at a hawker centre, then a train to almost anywhere you need to be.

candidates.name: Johor Bahru
candidates.summary: Johor Bahru is easiest to appreciate when you give it a life of its own.

candidates.name: Dijon
candidates.summary: In Dijon, the covered market can give the week its shape.

candidates.name: Joinville
candidates.summary: Joinville’s pleasures are often found between the headline attractions: coffee and cake, a meal along one of its restaurant streets, or a walk that reveals another piece of the city’s cultural history.

candidates.name: Concepción
candidates.summary: The university campus, Parque Ecuador and the streets around Plaza Perú give Concepción a lively, lived-in character.

candidates.name: Nagoya
candidates.summary: Nagoya becomes more interesting when the question changes from what to photograph to where to spend an ordinary Tuesday.

candidates.name: Udine
candidates.summary: Udine’s scale becomes apparent in the space between a café in the center and the quieter streets where the day actually ends.

candidates.name: San Rafael
candidates.summary: San Rafael offers a city base for wine country, but the useful long-stay picture begins with the streets around the center rather than a vineyard terrace.

candidates.name: Charlottesville
candidates.summary: Charlottesville works best when its university-town image is tested against an ordinary week.

candidates.name: San Isidro de El General
candidates.summary: San Isidro de El General is a place to understand through errands: the municipal market, a bus connection, a café near a familiar landmark and the conversation needed to arrange a repair.

candidates.name: Aveiro
candidates.summary: Aveiro works best when the canals become part of an ordinary week rather than the entire reason for moving.

candidates.name: Zaragoza
candidates.summary: Zaragoza is an inland working city whose pleasures fit between ordinary errands: shopping at Mercado Central, an evening in El Tubo, or a walk toward the Ebro after the strongest heat has passed.

candidates.name: Innsbruck
candidates.summary: Innsbruck puts a mountain horizon behind a very real housing decision.

candidates.name: Natal
candidates.summary: Natal asks a long-stay resident to separate a coastal holiday image from the practical geography of a working city.

candidates.name: Angers
candidates.summary: Angers makes a long stay feel less like a circuit of châteaux and more like a sequence of manageable city days.

candidates.name: Roanoke
candidates.summary: Roanoke offers a useful middle ground between a small mountain town and a larger service center.

candidates.name: Cartago
candidates.summary: Cartago’s appeal is an everyday highland-city routine rather than a coastal escape.

candidates.name: Volos
candidates.summary: Volos is a working waterfront city, not an island holiday stretched into a lease.

candidates.name: Varaždin
candidates.summary: Varaždin offers a northern Croatian routine that is quite different from an Adriatic long stay.

candidates.name: Hsinchu
candidates.summary: Hsinchu City is easier to understand as several daily routines than as one technology-city label.

candidates.name: Las Tablas
candidates.summary: Las Tablas rewards a different kind of long stay from a beach resort.

candidates.name: Manta
candidates.summary: Manta’s shoreline is only one part of the city.

candidates.name: Nuremberg
candidates.summary: Nuremberg becomes more interesting as a place to live when you stop organizing every day around the castle.

candidates.name: Strasbourg
candidates.summary: Strasbourg offers a convincing everyday life beyond the photograph of Petite France.

candidates.name: Kaunas
candidates.summary: Kaunas asks you to pay attention to levels as well as distances.

candidates.name: Aguascalientes
candidates.summary: Aguascalientes is an inland city with historic barrios, railway heritage and the seasonal San Marcos fair.

candidates.name: Galway
candidates.summary: Galway combines a compact cultural center, university life and an Atlantic waterfront.

candidates.name: Ann Arbor
candidates.summary: Ann Arbor offers university museums, distinct downtown districts and a strong local-food setting.

candidates.name: Izola
candidates.summary: Izola retains a compact fishing-town and Venetian-heritage setting on Slovenia’s coast.

candidates.name: Takamatsu
candidates.summary: Takamatsu combines a Seto Inland Sea port, garden and museum outings, shopping arcades and Sanuki food culture.

candidates.name: Cuernavaca
candidates.summary: Cuernavaca offers historic gardens, museums and established urban services in Morelos.

candidates.name: El Valle de Antón
candidates.summary: El Valle de Antón is an inland valley base for markets, birdwatching and trail outings.

candidates.name: Bentonville
candidates.summary: Bentonville combines art institutions, a central dining district and a strong cycling identity.

candidates.name: Canberra
candidates.summary: Canberra offers national cultural institutions and distinct residential precincts around Lake Burley Griffin.

candidates.name: Zagreb
candidates.summary: Zagreb offers an inland capital-city lifestyle with markets, museums and an extensive public-transport network.

candidates.name: Viña del Mar
candidates.summary: Viña del Mar combines Pacific promenades, gardens and an established urban service base.

candidates.name: Trento
candidates.summary: Trento offers a compact historic center, university activity and an Alpine-valley base with museums and regional transport.

candidates.name: Heredia
candidates.summary: Heredia offers a university-city base with a compact historic center and a wider metropolitan housing market.

candidates.name: Brașov
candidates.summary: Brașov combines a historic center with larger residential districts and access to mountain outings.

candidates.name: Luang Prabang
candidates.summary: Luang Prabang is a heritage-city base at the Mekong and Nam Khan, suited to deliberate cultural routines rather than big-city service expectations.

candidates.name: Ensenada
candidates.summary: Ensenada combines an urban Pacific port with seafood culture and access to wine-country excursions.

candidates.name: Cluj-Napoca
candidates.summary: Cluj-Napoca offers university-city culture, parks and a substantial urban services base.

candidates.name: Tampere
candidates.summary: Tampere combines industrial heritage, lake landscapes and a daily transit network.

candidates.name: Rennes
candidates.summary: Rennes combines a historic centre, food markets, cultural institutions and a metropolitan transport network.

candidates.name: York
candidates.summary: York offers a compact historic core, rail heritage and a large visitor economy.

candidates.name: Encarnación
candidates.summary: Encarnación offers a Paraná riverfront routine alongside a central shopping district and residential areas with different travel needs.

candidates.name: Nara
candidates.summary: Nara supports a cultural routine around temples and parkland, but a long-stay address should also work for groceries, healthcare and rail journeys.

candidates.name: Regensburg
candidates.summary: Regensburg combines a historic Danube core with residential districts beyond the most visited lanes.

candidates.name: Siem Reap
candidates.summary: Siem Reap can support a cultural long stay, but temple excursions, everyday city errands and medical contingency planning are different needs.

candidates.name: Vitória
candidates.summary: Vitória combines historic island districts with mainland residential areas.

candidates.name: Asunción
candidates.summary: Asunción pairs a historic river-facing center with newer residential and commercial districts farther east.

candidates.name: La Serena
candidates.summary: La Serena combines a historic inland center with coastal apartment districts.

candidates.name: Coronado
candidates.summary: Coronado is a Pacific resort-residential setting where beach homes, condominium complexes and the highway commercial corridor create different daily routines.

candidates.name: Salerno
candidates.summary: Salerno combines a compact medieval core, a seafront urban routine and residential districts extending east.

candidates.name: Morelia
candidates.summary: Morelia offers a substantial historic center, university and cultural life, and contrasting residential settings beyond the central monuments.

candidates.name: Tbilisi
candidates.summary: Tbilisi is a river-valley capital where a hillside heritage core, broad central avenues and residential districts offer different daily routines.

candidates.name: Rethymno
candidates.summary: Rethymno combines a compact historic core with modern residential streets and eastern coastal neighborhoods.

candidates.name: Nantes
candidates.summary: Nantes offers a working urban base with cultural venues, markets and distinct residential districts.

candidates.name: San Diego
candidates.summary: San Diego offers urban neighborhoods, cultural parks and coastal settings within a large municipality.

candidates.name: Jeju City
candidates.summary: Jeju City is the northern urban base of Jeju Island, with an older civic core, newer commercial neighborhoods and an airport-side coast.

candidates.name: Edinburgh
candidates.summary: Edinburgh offers distinct old-town, Georgian, port and seaside residential settings.

candidates.name: Christchurch
candidates.summary: Christchurch housing searches span the rebuilt center, established suburbs, hills and coast.

candidates.name: Utrecht
candidates.summary: Utrecht combines a canal-centered historic core with residential districts and a major rail interchange.

candidates.name: Hanoi
candidates.summary: Hanoi combines a dense historic core, lakeside search areas and a much larger municipal territory.

candidates.name: Mexico City
candidates.summary: Mexico City rewards a neighborhood-based long stay rather than constant cross-city journeys.

candidates.name: Graz
candidates.summary: Graz combines a historic center, university districts and a design-oriented west bank.

candidates.name: Ponta Delgada
candidates.summary: Ponta Delgada is an island-city base on São Miguel.

candidates.name: Québec City
candidates.summary: Québec City offers distinct upper- and lower-town routines, French-language daily life and a strong seasonal contrast.

candidates.name: Seville
candidates.summary: Seville combines a compact heritage core with distinct residential districts on both sides of the river.

candidates.name: Lyon
candidates.summary: Lyon offers contrasting historic riverfront, hill and neighborhood-center routines.

candidates.name: Colonia del Sacramento
candidates.summary: Colonia rewards a slower riverfront routine and repeated visits to its historic quarter.

candidates.name: Leiden
candidates.summary: Leiden combines a compact university-city center with a major rail hub and medical campus.

candidates.name: Salta
candidates.summary: Salta offers a historic civic center, museums and a strong regional cultural identity.

candidates.name: Pula
candidates.summary: Pula combines Roman monuments and an ordinary working city with a strongly seasonal visitor economy.

candidates.name: Grecia
candidates.summary: Grecia offers a central market and civic core within a much broader canton.

candidates.name: Cádiz
candidates.summary: Cádiz offers a compact historic-city routine beside the Atlantic, with markets and cultural sites close enough to revisit rather than tick off once.

candidates.name: Heidelberg
candidates.summary: Heidelberg is more than an attractive old town: the university, medical campus and residential districts create different daily routines.

candidates.name: Puerto Varas
candidates.summary: Puerto Varas offers a lake-oriented urban base with heritage streets and regional excursions, but it should not be confused with neighboring Frutillar or with the much wider commune.

candidates.name: Nagano
candidates.summary: Nagano combines a station-centered urban routine with Zenkoji temple culture and a municipality extending into mountain districts.

candidates.name: Antigua Guatemala
candidates.summary: Antigua Guatemala combines a compact historic centre, named church and convent sites, cafés and surrounding village communities.

candidates.name: Perth
candidates.summary: Perth combines Swan River city life with a much wider coastal metropolitan area.

candidates.name: Cork
candidates.summary: Cork offers a compact food-and-culture centre around the River Lee, with residential choices extending into hillier and more suburban districts.

candidates.name: Turin
candidates.summary: Turin offers a dense urban routine built around museums, arcades, markets and public transport.

candidates.name: Escazú
candidates.summary: Escazú is a varied canton west of San José, not one uniform expat neighbourhood.

candidates.name: Puebla
candidates.summary: Puebla offers a historic urban setting with museums, regional cooking and residential barrios around the central grid.

candidates.name: Split
candidates.summary: Split combines a lived-in historic core, working port and residential districts around the Marjan peninsula and eastern coast.

candidates.name: Cebu City
candidates.summary: Cebu City pairs business districts and major shopping complexes with an older heritage centre and upland residential areas.

candidates.name: Halifax
candidates.summary: Halifax offers harbour-oriented city life, cultural institutions and residential districts with different relationships to the downtown core.

candidates.name: Wellington
candidates.summary: Wellington combines a compact capital-city centre with waterfront cultural life and hillside residential districts.

candidates.name: Charleston
candidates.summary: Charleston offers an unusually rich historic urban setting and a strong dining scene.

candidates.name: Kota Kinabalu
candidates.summary: Kota Kinabalu is a compact coastal gateway to Sabah, with markets and city services distinct from island and mountain excursions.

candidates.name: Montpellier
candidates.summary: Montpellier pairs a medieval centre with planned districts extending toward the Lez.

candidates.name: Victoria
candidates.summary: Victoria offers a compact harbour city with distinctive residential districts and access to Vancouver Island.

candidates.name: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
candidates.summary: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria offers two distinct starting points for a longer stay: the historic Vegueta–Triana core and the northern beach-and-port districts.

candidates.name: La Rochelle
candidates.summary: La Rochelle is a maritime city whose Old Port, historical streets and cultural venues can support a longer stay beyond a summer itinerary.

candidates.name: Freiburg im Breisgau
candidates.summary: Freiburg im Breisgau combines a historic core with distinct residential quarters and the Black Forest edge.

candidates.name: Viseu
candidates.summary: Viseu is an inland city whose historic core, public gardens and Dão cultural setting offer a different long-stay proposition from Portugal’s beach cities.

candidates.name: Taichung
candidates.summary: Taichung’s central urban districts provide several different long-stay settings: historic commerce in Central District, museums and greenway activity in West District, shopping and university-related activity in North District, and the theater and newer commercial areas of Xitun.

candidates.name: Hobart
candidates.summary: Hobart combines a working-waterfront city center, Salamanca’s visitor activity and Battery Point’s historic residential setting.

candidates.name: La Paz
candidates.summary: La Paz pairs a bayfront promenade with a compact cultural center in Baja California Sur.

candidates.name: Querétaro
candidates.summary: Santiago de Querétaro offers an inland historic-city setting organized around plazas, cultural buildings and the aqueduct.

candidates.name: Bologna
candidates.summary: Bologna’s food markets, porticoes and museums provide a practical framework for a long stay.

candidates.name: Medellín
candidates.summary: Medellín’s official visitor material distinguishes Laureles, El Poblado and Ciudad del Río rather than presenting one uniform urban lifestyle.

candidates.name: Bangkok
candidates.summary: Bangkok combines a large urban transport network with distinct historic and contemporary districts. Plan around actual daily journeys rather than treating the whole metropolis as one interchangeable neighborhood.

candidates.name: Barcelona
candidates.summary: Barcelona combines markets, cultural institutions and distinct urban districts. Eixample, Gracia, Poblenou and the old-city market areas offer different starting points for a longer stay.

candidates.name: San Miguel de Allende
candidates.summary: San Miguel de Allende offers a heritage-centered cultural setting with named galleries, a public library and local dining. Separate the historic town from surrounding excursions and municipality-wide statistics.

candidates.name: Atenas
candidates.summary: Atenas requires a clear distinction between the central town and the wider canton. A property advertised as Atenas may sit in a different district with a substantially different daily routine.

candidates.name: Málaga
candidates.summary: A Mediterranean city combining a historic cultural center, distinct urban beaches and varied residential districts; housing, noise and access differ substantially by address.

candidates.name: Bariloche
candidates.summary: A Patagonian lake city framed by the Andes, combining a real urban center with skiing, hiking, beaches, craft beer, chocolate and year-round outdoor access.

candidates.name: Mendoza
candidates.summary: A leafy Andean city built around wine, wide boulevards, parks and café culture, with strong everyday services and easy access to Argentina’s premier vineyard region.

candidates.name: João Pessoa
candidates.summary: A relaxed northeastern Brazilian capital with urban beaches, a long waterfront promenade, strong value, tropical weather and more everyday infrastructure than a resort town.

candidates.name: Punta del Este
candidates.summary: Uruguay’s polished Atlantic resort city, balancing calm bay beaches and open-ocean surf with high-rise living, restaurants, marinas and a highly seasonal social calendar.

candidates.name: Ghent
candidates.summary: A compact Flemish university city with canals, medieval architecture, cycling, restaurants and a car-light center that delivers big-city culture at a human scale.

candidates.name: Wānaka
candidates.summary: A fast-growing South Island lake town with immediate access to mountains, hiking, skiing and water recreation, plus a polished café scene and strong outdoor community.

candidates.name: Stellenbosch
candidates.summary: A historic Cape Winelands university town combining oak-lined streets, acclaimed restaurants and wine estates with mountain trails and quick access to Cape Town.

candidates.name: Loreto
candidates.summary: A small Sea of Cortez town with a historic mission center, marine park, fishing, calm-water recreation and direct access to the dramatic Sierra de la Giganta.

candidates.name: Vevey
candidates.summary: A compact French-speaking city on Lake Geneva with a walkable waterfront, culture, rail access and vineyard scenery, pairing Swiss infrastructure with a relaxed Riviera setting.

candidates.name: Hakuba
candidates.summary: A Japanese Alps village surrounded by major ski areas, mountain trails and onsen culture, with a growing international community and dramatic four-season scenery.

candidates.name: Whistler
candidates.summary: A purpose-built alpine resort town where skiing, mountain biking, lakes, golf and a walkable village support a highly active year-round lifestyle.

candidates.name: Bansko
candidates.summary: A historic Bulgarian mountain town at the foot of the Pirin range, combining a major ski area with a compact old center, lower costs and four-season outdoor access.

candidates.name: Pucón
candidates.summary: A compact Chilean lake town beneath Villarrica volcano, built around outdoor adventure, hot springs, national parks and a lively tourism-centered center.

candidates.name: Noosa Heads
candidates.summary: A polished Sunshine Coast beach town where Main Beach, Hastings Street and Noosa National Park create a walkable core with strong dining and outdoor appeal.

candidates.name: Baden-Baden
candidates.summary: An elegant Black Forest spa city centered on thermal baths, parks, museums, classical culture and a compact urban core with strong access to nature.

candidates.name: Sarajevo
candidates.summary: Sarajevo is a dramatic valley capital ringed by Olympic mountains, combining Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian heritage, café culture, affordability, skiing and hiking with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Da Lat
candidates.summary: Da Lat is a pine-covered Vietnamese highland city built around lakes, gardens and cool uplands, combining mild climate, coffee culture, food, flowers, waterfalls and low day-to-day costs with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Sète
candidates.summary: Sète is a working Mediterranean port threaded by canals between the sea and Étang de Thau, combining beaches, seafood, markets, rail access, canals and authentic year-round city life with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Tainan
candidates.summary: Tainan is Taiwan’s old capital, dense with temples, lanes, night markets and low-rise neighborhoods, combining food, healthcare, rail links, safety, cycling and cultural depth with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Arequipa
candidates.summary: Arequipa is a high-altitude white-stone city beneath El Misti volcano, combining UNESCO architecture, food, sunny dry climate, hospitals and access to Colca Canyon with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Sibiu
candidates.summary: Sibiu is a compact Transylvanian city of fortified squares, tiled roofs and nearby Carpathians, combining walkability, culture, low costs, festivals, safety and mountain access with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Ohrid
candidates.summary: Ohrid is a UNESCO lake city of churches, stone lanes and mountain-backed water, combining Lake Ohrid, affordability, history, swimming, cafés and compact scale with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Kuching
candidates.summary: Kuching is a relaxed Borneo capital on the Sarawak River with rainforests and wildlife close by, combining food, English usability, healthcare, value, cultural mix and access to national parks with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Ipoh
candidates.summary: Ipoh is a Malaysian heritage city surrounded by dramatic limestone karsts, combining food, low costs, hospitals, rail access, cave temples and manageable urban scale with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Dunedin
candidates.summary: Dunedin is a hilly southern university city with Victorian architecture and wildlife-rich coastline, combining culture, healthcare, university energy, beaches, wildlife and cooler climate with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Sucre
candidates.summary: Sucre is a graceful highland capital of white colonial facades and university life, combining architecture, mild days, affordability, language schools and slower pace with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Loja
candidates.summary: Loja is a temperate Andean city known for music, universities and nearby cloud-forest landscapes, combining mild climate, low costs, dollar economy, walkable center and access to Podocarpus with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Campeche
candidates.summary: Campeche is a walled UNESCO city on the Gulf of Mexico with pastel streets and a broad malecón, combining colonial beauty, lower costs, walkability, food and relaxed Gulf lifestyle with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Oberstdorf
candidates.summary: Oberstdorf is a polished Bavarian alpine town beneath the Allgäu peaks, combining skiing, hiking, rail access, healthcare quality, pedestrian center and immaculate infrastructure with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Frutillar
candidates.summary: Frutillar is a German-influenced lakeside town facing snowcapped Osorno volcano, combining Lake Llanquihue, music, walkability, scenery, calmer pace and Puerto Varas/Puerto Montt access with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Launceston
candidates.summary: Launceston is a compact northern Tasmanian city at the gateway to wine country and Cataract Gorge, combining food, cooler climate, hospitals, vineyards, walkable center and outdoor access with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Sandpoint
candidates.summary: Sandpoint is a small Idaho lake town with Schweitzer Mountain rising directly above Lake Pend Oreille, combining skiing, boating, walkable downtown, trails, community events and U.S. familiarity with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Nelson
candidates.summary: Nelson is a sunny upper-South-Island city between Tasman Bay, vineyards and national parks, combining arts, beaches, cycling, markets, wineries and Abel Tasman access with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Albany
candidates.summary: Albany is a historic port city on Western Australia’s wild southern coast, combining beaches, national parks, whale watching, cooler climate, food and strong small-city services with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Essaouira
candidates.summary: Essaouira is a blue-and-white Atlantic medina wrapped by ramparts, fishing port and broad windswept beach, combining art, seafood, walkability, surf, mild temperatures and strong visual character with enough everyday infrastructure for serious long stays.

candidates.name: Almuñécar
candidates.summary: Almuñécar pairs a walkable Andalusian old town with a long Costa Tropical waterfront, subtropical gardens, Moorish fortifications and easy day-to-day beach life without the scale or resort intensity of Málaga.

candidates.name: Tavira
candidates.summary: Tavira is an elegant eastern-Algarve town on the Gilão River, with tiled streets, a castle ridge, ferry-linked island beaches and a calmer year-round rhythm than the Algarve’s larger resort centers.

candidates.name: Kalamata
candidates.summary: Kalamata combines a real Greek regional city, a long swimmable seafront, serious food culture and direct access to the Taygetos mountains, giving it more year-round substance than a small island resort.

candidates.name: Pak Nam Pran
candidates.summary: Pak Nam Pran is the quieter coastal alternative south of Hua Hin: a low-rise beach community of fishing villages, mangroves, kite-surfing and seafood with Sam Roi Yot’s limestone landscape close by.

candidates.name: Piriápolis
candidates.summary: Piriápolis is a small Uruguayan beach city with a broad rambla, early-20th-century resort architecture, walkable services and low hills behind the coast, offering a calmer alternative to Punta del Este.

candidates.name: Plovdiv
candidates.summary: Plovdiv layers Roman ruins, Ottoman-era houses, Kapana’s creative district and a large everyday Bulgarian city into one of Europe’s most compelling value-oriented long-stay bases.

candidates.name: Dénia
candidates.summary: Dénia combines a working Mediterranean port, castle-topped historic center, long sandy beaches, rocky coves and UNESCO-recognized gastronomy beneath the Montgó massif.

candidates.name: Viana do Castelo
candidates.summary: Viana do Castelo combines a handsome Minho historic center, Lima River waterfront, Atlantic beaches and the Santa Luzia hillside with a cooler, greener climate than southern Portugal.

candidates.name: Pézenas
candidates.summary: Pézenas is a small Languedoc market town of hôtels particuliers, artisan workshops, Molière associations and café-lined stone streets, close enough to Mediterranean beaches without being a beach resort.

candidates.name: Matsuyama
candidates.summary: Matsuyama blends one of Japan’s finest original castles, the historic Dōgo Onsen district, streetcars and a livable Shikoku regional-city scale, with lower pressure and costs than Tokyo or Kyoto.

candidates.name: Taitung
candidates.summary: Taitung is Taiwan’s slower Pacific-side city, framed by mountains and ocean with Indigenous culture, cycling, hot springs and open landscapes that feel radically different from Taipei’s density.

candidates.name: Quy Nhon
candidates.summary: Quy Nhon is a long, curving Vietnamese beach city with a strong seafood culture, Cham heritage and easy coastal access, still feeling more local and lower-key than Da Nang or Nha Trang.

candidates.name: Herceg Novi
candidates.summary: Herceg Novi terraces down to the Bay of Kotor in layers of stone stairs, fortresses, gardens and waterfront promenades, with a milder, greener feel than much of Montenegro’s coast.

candidates.name: Fethiye
candidates.summary: Fethiye is a Turkish Mediterranean harbor city with a real year-round center, Lycian archaeology, marinas and access to Ölüdeniz, Babadağ and the Lycian Way.

candidates.name: St. George
candidates.summary: St. George is a fast-growing red-rock city with golf, trail systems, strong healthcare and immediate access to Snow Canyon, trading mild winters for very hot summers and a car-oriented layout.

candidates.name: Coeur d'Alene
candidates.summary: Coeur d'Alene pairs a polished lakefront downtown with Tubbs Hill trails, boating and four-season Inland Northwest scenery, while Spokane supplies big-city air access and deeper services nearby.

candidates.name: San Luis Obispo
candidates.summary: San Luis Obispo combines a genuinely walkable Central Coast downtown, Cal Poly energy, weekly farmers markets and immediate hill trails, with beaches and Edna Valley wine country minutes away.

candidates.name: Flagstaff
candidates.summary: Flagstaff combines pine forest, volcanic terrain, a lively historic downtown and a university town sitting above 6,900 feet with the San Francisco Peaks on the skyline, with a lifestyle that particularly suits active adults and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Ashland
candidates.summary: Ashland combines a compact arts town where Lithia Park reaches into downtown, theater drives the cultural calendar and trails climb quickly toward the Siskiyous, with a lifestyle that particularly suits theater lovers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Whitefish
candidates.summary: Whitefish combines a polished but still outdoors-first mountain town where a working rail stop, a walkable downtown, Whitefish Lake and a major ski mountain all sit within the same compact lifestyle orbit, with a lifestyle that particularly suits skiers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Saratoga Springs
candidates.summary: Saratoga Springs combines a handsome upstate city whose identity blends horse racing, mineral springs, performing arts, college energy and a downtown that is active well beyond summer visitors, with a lifestyle that particularly suits culture-minded retirees and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Annapolis
candidates.summary: Annapolis combines a compact state capital where brick colonial streets meet a working harbor, the Naval Academy, sailing culture and a restaurant scene that spills toward City Dock, with a lifestyle that particularly suits sailors and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Wilmington
candidates.summary: Wilmington combines a riverfront city with a real historic downtown, a growing food-and-creative scene and three distinct beach communities close enough to shape daily life without turning Wilmington into a pure resort town, with a lifestyle that particularly suits beach lovers who still want a city and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: St. Augustine
candidates.summary: St. Augustine combines the nation's oldest continuously occupied European-founded city paired with Atlantic beaches, live music, old neighborhoods and enough year-round tourism to keep the center animated, with a lifestyle that particularly suits history fans and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Hilton Head Island
candidates.summary: Hilton Head Island combines a low-rise barrier island where beach access, bike paths, golf and manicured residential communities define the lifestyle more than a traditional downtown, with a lifestyle that particularly suits golfers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Traverse City
candidates.summary: Traverse City combines a small Great Lakes city with a surprisingly sophisticated restaurant scene, bayfront beaches, wineries on two peninsulas and a downtown that stays useful after vacation season, with a lifestyle that particularly suits food-and-wine travelers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Delray Beach
candidates.summary: Delray Beach combines a beach city with a genuine walkable entertainment spine: Atlantic Avenue ties restaurants, galleries and nightlife to the ocean in a way many South Florida communities do not, with a lifestyle that particularly suits beach-focused retirees and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Lagos
candidates.summary: Lagos combines a compact Algarve town where golden cliffs, coves, a walled historic center and an active marina create far more year-round texture than a purpose-built beach resort, with a lifestyle that particularly suits sun-seeking retirees and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Chiang Rai
candidates.summary: Chiang Rai combines a laid-back northern Thai city whose temples, art, coffee culture and surrounding mountains make it feel creative and regionally distinctive without Chiang Mai's scale, with a lifestyle that particularly suits slow travelers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Guanajuato
candidates.summary: Guanajuato combines a theatrical UNESCO hill city of tunnels, plazas, university life and brightly stacked neighborhoods where culture is not a district but the city’s operating system, with a lifestyle that particularly suits arts and festival lovers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Newport
candidates.summary: Newport combines a compact sailing city where Gilded Age architecture, a working harbor, festivals and coastal walks create genuine urban energy inside a small New England footprint, with a lifestyle that particularly suits sailors and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Cascais
candidates.summary: Cascais combines an Atlantic town that combines beaches, a polished historic center, surfing, golf and an easy rail link to Lisbon, giving it both resort atmosphere and metropolitan practicality, with a lifestyle that particularly suits international retirees and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Hood River
candidates.summary: Hood River combines a wind-and-water sports hub surrounded by orchards, wineries, waterfalls and Mount Hood, with enough breweries and restaurants to feel far more energetic than its population suggests, with a lifestyle that particularly suits windsurfers and kiteboarders and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Eureka Springs
candidates.summary: Eureka Springs combines a steep, eccentric Victorian mountain town where art galleries, live music, LGBTQ-friendly events, springs and winding streets create a bohemian destination unlike the surrounding Ozarks, with a lifestyle that particularly suits artists and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: New Hope
candidates.summary: New Hope combines a tiny but high-energy Delaware River town where theater, galleries, restaurants, nightlife and a walkable bridge to Lambertville create an outsized weekend and arts scene, with a lifestyle that particularly suits arts lovers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Healdsburg
candidates.summary: Healdsburg combines a polished Sonoma wine-country town where an elegant plaza, destination restaurants, tasting rooms and the Russian River sit inside a genuinely walkable small-city core, with a lifestyle that particularly suits food and wine travelers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Bocas del Toro
candidates.summary: Bocas del Toro combines a colorful Caribbean island town where water taxis function like buses, surf breaks and beaches replace suburban amenities, and an international traveler/expat scene keeps the waterfront lively, with a lifestyle that particularly suits divers and travelers who want a destination with real everyday texture.

candidates.name: Tivat
candidates.summary: Tivat is a compact Bay of Kotor town transformed by the redevelopment of a former naval base into Porto Montenegro, a polished marina district of yachts, promenades, hotels and restaurants. Beyond the luxury waterfront, Kalimanj harbor, the old naval heritage and nearby Vrmac Peninsula preserve a more local coastal character. Its airport, flat center and central bay location make Tivat one of Montenegro’s easiest bases.

candidates.name: Matera
candidates.summary: Matera rises from a limestone ravine in a sculptural maze of cave houses, rock churches, stairways and terraces. The Sassi districts appear ancient because they are: people have occupied this landscape for millennia. Today restored caves hold homes, museums, restaurants and hotels, but the city’s raw geology and difficult social history remain visible beneath the cinematic beauty.

candidates.name: Trieste
candidates.summary: Trieste is an Adriatic port city with Vienna’s architectural manners, Slavic undertones and a fiercely local coffeehouse culture. Piazza Unità d’Italia opens directly to the sea, while steep streets climb toward the Karst Plateau. Habsburg palaces, literary cafés, Orthodox churches and working docks give the city a borderland identity unlike anywhere else in Italy.

candidates.name: Braga
candidates.summary: Braga combines baroque churches, granite streets, leafy squares and a large student population in the green Minho region of northern Portugal. The city is deeply associated with Portuguese Catholic tradition, yet its cafés, university neighborhoods and expanding technology sector keep it from feeling frozen in history.

candidates.name: Valencia
candidates.summary: Valencia combines Mediterranean beaches, a dense historic center and the futuristic architecture of the City of Arts and Sciences within one remarkably livable urban fabric. The former Turia riverbed now forms a ribbon of parks and cycling paths across the city, connecting neighborhoods, museums, sports facilities and the coast.

candidates.name: Rijeka
candidates.summary: Rijeka is Croatia’s principal working port, a city of Habsburg façades, shipyards, steep neighborhoods and a creative scene that feels more urban and unvarnished than the country’s resort towns. Korzo serves as the social spine, while Trsat Castle watches over Kvarner Bay from the hills above.

candidates.name: Zadar
candidates.summary: Zadar layers Roman streets, medieval churches and contemporary waterfront art on a compact peninsula facing the islands of northern Dalmatia. At sunset, waves play the Sea Organ beneath marble steps while the nearby Greeting to the Sun turns the promenade into a glowing public stage.

candidates.name: Piran
candidates.summary: Piran is a tightly packed Venetian-style town at the tip of Slovenia’s short Adriatic coast. Terracotta roofs rise from Tartini Square toward St. George’s Church, while stone lanes descend to a fishing harbor and sea walls. Its scale, architecture and car-light center give it the intimacy of a carefully preserved maritime village.

candidates.name: Rovinj
candidates.summary: Rovinj rises from the western Istrian coast in a tight spiral of stone lanes crowned by the bell tower of St. Euphemia. Once an island, the old town still feels maritime at every turn, with fishing boats in the harbor, pastel Venetian façades and glimpses of blue water between buildings. Outside the historic core, pine-shaded coves and Zlatni Rt forest park soften the resort atmosphere with easy access to swimming and cycling.

candidates.name: Kanazawa
candidates.summary: Kanazawa is a refined castle city on Japan’s Sea of Japan coast, known for Kenroku-en Garden, preserved samurai and geisha districts, contemporary art and exceptional traditional crafts. It offers much of Kyoto’s cultural depth in a smaller, less overwhelming setting, with gold leaf, Kaga cuisine and carefully maintained historic neighborhoods shaping its identity.

candidates.name: Polignano a Mare
candidates.summary: Polignano a Mare clings to limestone cliffs above the Adriatic, with whitewashed lanes, sea caves and balconies overlooking impossibly blue water. Lama Monachile, the town’s narrow pebble cove beneath a Roman bridge, is the signature view, but the real pleasure lies in the compact old town and the constant presence of the sea.

candidates.name: Cefalù
candidates.summary: Cefalù is a compact Sicilian seaside town where a golden Norman cathedral, medieval lanes and a broad sandy beach sit beneath the massive limestone profile of La Rocca. The town manages to combine a genuine historic center with one of Sicily’s most accessible beach settings, which explains both its enduring popularity and its heavy summer crowds.

candidates.name: Taormina
candidates.summary: Taormina occupies a dramatic terrace above Sicily’s Ionian coast, where the ancient theater frames views of Mount Etna and the sea. Corso Umberto, flowered balconies, elegant hotels and the cable car down to Mazzarò and Isola Bella create a polished resort atmosphere that has attracted international travelers since the Grand Tour.

candidates.name: Podgorica
candidates.summary: Podgorica is a low-rise Balkan capital spread across the Morača and Ribnica rivers, with broad boulevards, café culture and a fragmented mix of Ottoman remains, Yugoslav-era planning and new commercial districts. It lacks the postcard drama of Montenegro’s coast, but it functions as the country’s practical transport, administrative and business hub.

candidates.name: Kotor
candidates.summary: Kotor is a fortified medieval town compressed between the dark mountains of the Dinaric Alps and the deep blue waters of its namesake bay. Inside the walls, polished stone lanes lead to Romanesque churches, Venetian palaces and tiny squares, while the steep path to San Giovanni Fortress reveals one of the Adriatic’s most dramatic panoramas.

candidates.name: Bergamo
candidates.summary: Bergamo is a prosperous Lombardy city split between the modern Città Bassa and the walled Città Alta, which rises above it on a hilltop of cobbled lanes, Romanesque churches and elegant piazzas. A pair of funiculars and the UNESCO-listed Venetian walls turn the city’s vertical geography into part of the experience.

candidates.name: Pietrasanta
candidates.summary: Pietrasanta is a small Tuscan art town between the Apuan Alps and the Versilia coast, where marble workshops, bronze foundries and contemporary galleries sit around a refined medieval center. Known as the “Little Athens” of Italy, it feels less like a resort and more like a working international studio community.

candidates.name: Alicante
candidates.summary: Alicante is a bright Mediterranean city built around Postiguet Beach, a palm-lined esplanade and the rocky height of Santa Bárbara Castle. Its compact center combines a working Spanish city, busy marina, university population and easy access to the resort towns of the Costa Blanca. | Alicante is a sunny Mediterranean city with beaches, a major airport and lower costs than Madrid or Barcelona.

candidates.name: Verona
candidates.summary: Verona is a richly layered northern Italian city where a Roman amphitheater, medieval bridges, Renaissance palaces and riverside neighborhoods coexist within a compact historic center. The Arena’s summer opera season gives the city an international cultural presence far beyond its association with Romeo and Juliet.

candidates.name: Radovljica
candidates.summary: A graceful Upper Carniolan town with a beautifully preserved medieval core, strong food traditions and the Julian Alps filling the horizon.

candidates.name: Osaka
candidates.summary: Japan's great food-and-commerce metropolis: fast, funny, energetic and remarkably easy to live in without a car.

candidates.name: Sitges
candidates.summary: A polished Mediterranean beach town with a walkable historic center, serious food, arts heritage and one of Spain's most visible LGBTQ social scenes.

candidates.name: Estepona
candidates.summary: A flower-filled Costa del Sol town that has become noticeably more polished while keeping a more relaxed residential feel than nearby Marbella.

candidates.name: Bled
candidates.summary: Slovenia's iconic alpine-lake town: exceptionally beautiful, easy to walk around and highly seasonal.

candidates.name: Olbia
candidates.summary: Sardinia's practical northeastern hub: a real working city with an airport, port and access to extraordinary beaches.

candidates.name: Hiroshima
candidates.summary: A highly livable regional capital where rivers, trams, food and modern daily life sit alongside some of the world's most important peace-history sites.

candidates.name: Kobe
candidates.summary: A cosmopolitan port city squeezed dramatically between Osaka Bay and the Rokko mountains, with excellent rail access and a calmer rhythm than Osaka.

candidates.name: Alghero
candidates.summary: A fortified Sardinian seaside city with Catalan character, walkable walls, beaches on the doorstep and one of the island's strongest long-stay settings.

candidates.name: Hakodate
candidates.summary: A compact southern-Hokkaido port with trams, seafood, historic hillside streets and one of Japan's great night views.

candidates.name: Desenzano del Garda
candidates.summary: Lake Garda's most practical southern-shore town, combining rail access, an active historic center, swimming and year-round services.

candidates.name: Onomichi
candidates.summary: A cinematic Seto Inland Sea port of hillside temples, narrow lanes and ferries, best known as the western gateway to the Shimanami Kaido.

candidates.name: Cartagena
candidates.summary: A substantial Mediterranean port city where Roman archaeology, naval history and ordinary regional life coexist without resort-town gloss.

candidates.name: Gijón
candidates.summary: A green Atlantic city with a broad urban beach, cider culture and a strong everyday-local feel.

candidates.name: Girona
candidates.summary: A compact Catalan city with medieval streets, riverfront architecture, serious food and some of Spain's best cycling access.

candidates.name: Ptuj
candidates.summary: Slovenia's oldest recorded town, centered on a hilltop castle, wine traditions, thermal baths and an unusually relaxed pace.

candidates.name: Koper
candidates.summary: Slovenia's main port city, blending a Venetian old center, bilingual coastal culture and immediate access to the country's short Adriatic shoreline.

candidates.name: Murcia
candidates.summary: A sunny regional capital with a strong university presence, excellent produce and noticeably lower everyday costs than Spain's headline coastal cities.

candidates.name: Takayama
candidates.summary: A beautifully preserved mountain city in the Japanese Alps, known for merchant streets, morning markets, festival culture and Hida beef.

candidates.name: Dubrovnik
candidates.summary: One of Europe's most spectacular walled cities, with immediate Adriatic swimming and extraordinary beauty paired with very real crowding and housing pressure.

candidates.name: Aomori
candidates.summary: A compact northern Japanese port city where serious snow, seafood, Nebuta culture and quick access to Hakkoda make everyday life feel distinctly Tohoku.

candidates.name: Kamakura
candidates.summary: A temple-rich coastal city south of Tokyo where surf beaches, wooded hills and an unusually walkable historic core create one of Japan’s most attractive small-city lifestyles.

candidates.name: Porto
candidates.summary: Portugal’s granite-and-azulejo northern capital pairs a dramatic Douro riverfront with walkable neighborhoods, serious food and wine, Atlantic beaches and excellent regional transport.

candidates.name: Kranj
candidates.summary: A compact Alpine gateway built above a river canyon, with a handsome old town, easy Ljubljana access and mountain recreation close enough to shape everyday life.

candidates.name: Coimbra
candidates.summary: Portugal’s historic university city combines a youthful academic pulse, monumental heritage and a calmer, more affordable daily rhythm than Lisbon or Porto.

candidates.name: Kumamoto
candidates.summary: A tram-friendly Kyushu regional capital anchored by its great castle, spring-fed gardens and easy access to Aso’s volcanic landscape.

candidates.name: Beppu
candidates.summary: Japan’s great hot-spring city, squeezed between Beppu Bay and volcanic mountains, where public baths and steam vents are part of ordinary neighborhood life.

candidates.name: Sapporo
candidates.summary: A full-scale northern metropolis with exceptional food, major-city services and genuine powder skiing less than an hour from downtown.

candidates.name: Lecce
candidates.summary: A honey-colored Baroque city in southern Puglia with elegant streets, excellent food and quick access to both Adriatic and Ionian beaches.

candidates.name: Athens
candidates.summary: A sprawling Mediterranean capital where world-class antiquity, late-night neighborhood life and improving urban culture sit beside heat, traffic and very real block-by-block differences.

candidates.name: Matsumoto
candidates.summary: A cultured mountain city with one of Japan’s great original castles and direct access to the Northern Alps, Kamikochi and serious winter sports.

candidates.name: Morioka
candidates.summary: A graceful Tohoku regional capital framed by Mount Iwate, known for craft traditions, three signature noodle styles and an easy Shinkansen connection to Tokyo.

candidates.name: Sendai
candidates.summary: Tohoku’s largest city balances major-city healthcare, universities and shopping with broad green boulevards, coastal access and mountain day trips.

candidates.name: Cavtat
candidates.summary: A polished harbor town south of Dubrovnik with clear-water swimming, a walkable waterfront and airport convenience, but a distinctly seasonal housing and service market.

candidates.name: Sirmione
candidates.summary: Lake Garda’s dramatic peninsula town combines thermal spas, waterfront walking and extraordinary scenery with heavy tourism and tight historic-center access.

candidates.name: Celje
candidates.summary: A practical Slovenian regional city with a lively old center, one of the country’s great castles and quick access to hills, spas and the Savinja Valley.

candidates.name: Nagasaki
candidates.summary: A steep, beautiful port city shaped by centuries of international exchange, with trams, extraordinary harbor views and one of Japan’s most distinctive urban identities.

candidates.name: Perugia
candidates.summary: Umbria’s hilltop capital mixes Etruscan and medieval streets with two universities, major festivals and a surprisingly youthful daily culture.

candidates.name: Novigrad
candidates.summary: A small Istrian fishing town with Venetian streets, easy swimming and excellent regional food, offering a calmer coastal alternative to Rovinj or Poreč.

candidates.name: Ioannina
candidates.summary: A youthful lake city in mountainous Epirus where Ottoman history, student energy and easy access to Zagori create a very different Greek lifestyle from the islands or Athens.

candidates.name: Siracusa
candidates.summary: Baroque-and-Greek waterfront city on Sicily’s southeast coast, with Ortigia lanes, archaeological depth, markets and easy sea access.

candidates.name: Toyama
candidates.summary: A polished Hokuriku city between Toyama Bay and the Japanese Alps, known for seafood, glass art and exceptional mountain access.

candidates.name: Kardamyli
candidates.summary: A stone-built Mani village where Taygetos mountains meet clear Messenian water, with hiking, swimming and a refined low-key atmosphere.

candidates.name: Trogir
candidates.summary: A compact UNESCO island old town near Split with Venetian stonework, a lively waterfront and easy airport access.

candidates.name: Korčula Town
candidates.summary: A fortified Adriatic town of limestone alleys, sea views and island culture, with beaches and vineyards close at hand.

candidates.name: Fukuoka
candidates.summary: A youthful, food-obsessed Japanese city with beaches, excellent transit, an international airport and an unusually relaxed big-city rhythm.

candidates.name: Maribor
candidates.summary: A relaxed Slovenian regional city on the Drava, with wine culture, a walkable center and Pohorje skiing at the urban edge.

candidates.name: Mali Lošinj
candidates.summary: A colorful island harbor surrounded by pine forest and clear Adriatic coves, with a strong wellness and boating identity.

candidates.name: Naha
candidates.summary: Okinawa’s compact capital blends subtropical island life, Ryukyuan culture, monorail convenience and an energetic food-and-market scene.

candidates.name: Niigata
candidates.summary: A spacious Sea of Japan port city known for rice, sake, seafood and easy access to snowy mountain country.

candidates.name: Kagoshima
candidates.summary: A southern Japanese city facing active Sakurajima, with ferries, hot springs, palm-lined streets and a distinctly volcanic landscape.

candidates.name: Bari
candidates.summary: Puglia’s energetic Adriatic capital mixes a working seafront, atmospheric old town, excellent food and strong regional transport.

candidates.name: Miyazaki
candidates.summary: A sunny southern Kyushu city with surf beaches, palms, shrines and an easygoing outdoor lifestyle.

candidates.name: Hvar Town
candidates.summary: A glamorous Dalmatian harbor town of limestone lanes, hillside views, boats and bright Adriatic water.

candidates.name: Oviedo
candidates.summary: Asturias’ elegant inland capital combines immaculate streets, cider culture, pre-Romanesque heritage and quick access to green mountains and coast.

candidates.name: Cagliari
candidates.summary: Sardinia’s lively capital offers a hilltop historic center, a long urban beach, markets and lagoon landscapes within one compact city.

candidates.name: Naxos Town
candidates.summary: A Cycladic port town with a Venetian old quarter, immediate beaches and a large island hinterland of villages and mountains.

candidates.name: Corfu Town
candidates.summary: A refined Ionian capital shaped by Venetian architecture, arcaded squares, fortresses and lush island scenery.

candidates.name: Thessaloniki
candidates.summary: Greece’s northern metropolis is a food-and-culture city on the Thermaic Gulf, with a huge waterfront, university energy and deep Byzantine history.

candidates.name: Okayama
candidates.summary: A sunny, practical western Japanese city anchored by Korakuen and Okayama Castle, with excellent rail access to the Setouchi region.

candidates.name: Chattanooga
candidates.summary: Riverfront Tennessee city framed by Lookout Mountain, with a revitalized downtown, serious outdoor access, and an unusually easygoing urban scale.

candidates.name: Greenville
candidates.summary: Compact Upstate city with a polished downtown, Falls Park at its center, a strong food scene, and easy Blue Ridge access.

candidates.name: Tucson
candidates.summary: Distinctive Sonoran Desert city with mountain-ringed views, UNESCO-recognized food culture, strong healthcare, and winter sunshine.

candidates.name: St. Petersburg
candidates.summary: Sunny Gulf Coast city with a walkable waterfront downtown, major museums, lively neighborhoods, and beaches just across the barrier islands.

candidates.name: Fort Collins
candidates.summary: Bike-friendly Front Range university city with a handsome Old Town, craft-beer culture, strong parks, and quick access to Horsetooth Reservoir.

candidates.name: Boise
candidates.summary: Fast-growing western capital with a lively downtown, Basque heritage, river greenbelt, foothill trails, and easy airport access.

candidates.name: Leiria
candidates.summary: Under-the-radar central Portuguese city with a castle above the old center, everyday services, lower pressure than Lisbon or Porto, and coast access.

candidates.name: Granada
candidates.summary: Andalusian university city where the Alhambra, Albaicín lanes, tapas culture, and Sierra Nevada access create unusual depth for its size.

candidates.name: Bilbao
candidates.summary: Prosperous Basque city with excellent transit, serious food and museum culture, green hills, and Atlantic beaches within the metro.

candidates.name: Osijek
candidates.summary: Affordable eastern Croatian river city with cycling paths, Austro-Hungarian architecture, café life, and a calmer pace than the Adriatic coast.

candidates.name: Vienna
candidates.summary: Highly livable Central European capital with world-class transit, museums, parks, coffeehouse culture, and unusually strong public services.

candidates.name: Ljubljana
candidates.summary: Green, compact capital built around a café-lined river, strong cycling, human-scale neighborhoods, and easy access to Slovenia’s mountains and coast.

candidates.name: Tallinn
candidates.summary: Digital-first Baltic capital where a medieval old town, creative districts, seaside neighborhoods, and efficient public services share a compact footprint.

candidates.name: Kuala Lumpur
candidates.summary: Modern Southeast Asian capital with excellent food, private healthcare, high-rise living, major air connections, and strong value for a large city.

candidates.name: Taipei
candidates.summary: Safe, transit-rich East Asian capital with exceptional food, mountain access, efficient healthcare, and neighborhoods that reward walking.

candidates.name: Busan
candidates.summary: Mountain-and-sea metropolis with urban beaches, seafood markets, strong transit, and a less intense pace than Seoul.

candidates.name: Adelaide
candidates.summary: Manageable Australian capital ringed by parklands, with beaches, festivals, strong healthcare, and wine regions at the edge of the metro.

candidates.name: Oaxaca
candidates.summary: Highland cultural capital built around markets, mezcal, extraordinary regional cooking, craft traditions, and a highly walkable historic center.

candidates.name: Pereira
candidates.summary: Coffee-region hub with springlike temperatures, modern services, strong regional access, and green mountain landscapes in every direction.

candidates.name: Salinas
candidates.summary: Pacific beach city on Ecuador’s Santa Elena peninsula with high-rise waterfront living, warm weather, and straightforward U.S.-dollar budgeting.

candidates.name: Asheville
candidates.summary: Blue Ridge mountain city with an unusually strong mix of arts, food, breweries, historic neighborhoods and quick access to serious outdoor recreation.

candidates.name: Portland
candidates.summary: Compact Maine port city with a walkable historic core, celebrated food scene, working waterfront and unusually easy access to islands and beaches.

candidates.name: Bend
candidates.summary: High-desert Oregon base where river trails, mountain sports, breweries and a lively downtown support an outdoors-first long-stay lifestyle.

candidates.name: Sarasota
candidates.summary: Gulf Coast city combining beaches, arts institutions, dining and strong retiree infrastructure with a polished, comfortable everyday feel.

candidates.name: Reno
candidates.summary: High-desert Nevada city with Tahoe access, a growing food and arts scene, university energy and no state individual income tax.

candidates.name: Salamanca
candidates.summary: Golden-stone university city with exceptional walkability, monumental architecture, youthful street life and comparatively approachable Spanish living costs.

candidates.name: San Sebastián
candidates.summary: Sophisticated Basque coastal city pairing extraordinary food, urban beaches, elegant neighborhoods and excellent walkability in a compact setting.

candidates.name: Évora
candidates.summary: UNESCO-listed Alentejo city with Roman and medieval layers, a walkable walled center, strong food culture and a slower inland Portuguese rhythm.

candidates.name: Prague
candidates.summary: Grand Central European capital with superb transit, architectural depth, lively neighborhoods and a daily cost structure still below many western peers.

candidates.name: Treviso
candidates.summary: Canal-laced Veneto city with elegant arcades, excellent food, cycling culture and easy rail access to Venice without Venice’s daily tourism pressure.

candidates.name: Annecy
candidates.summary: Alpine lake city with a postcard old town, extensive cycling and water recreation, mountain access and a polished French quality of life.

candidates.name: Ho Chi Minh City
candidates.summary: Fast-moving southern Vietnamese metropolis where food, cafés, modern services and relatively low daily costs meet intense traffic and tropical heat.

candidates.name: Tokyo
candidates.summary: Vast but remarkably orderly metropolis with world-class transit, exceptional food and services, deep neighborhood variety and near-frictionless daily convenience.

candidates.name: Bali
candidates.summary: Tropical Indonesian island offering beaches, temples, wellness, remote-work infrastructure and radically different lifestyles between its major districts.

candidates.name: Auckland
candidates.summary: Harbor-focused New Zealand metropolis with beaches, islands, multicultural food and strong services, balanced by high housing costs and traffic.

candidates.name: Cusco
candidates.summary: High-altitude Andean city where Inca foundations, colonial streets, markets and mountain access create one of Latin America’s most distinctive long-stay settings.

candidates.name: Valdivia
candidates.summary: River city in southern Chile with green landscapes, university culture, breweries, seafood and a cooler, wetter climate than most Latin American retirement hubs.

candidates.name: Córdoba
candidates.summary: Large Argentine university city with colonial architecture, energetic neighborhoods, healthcare depth and easy access to the Sierras de Córdoba.

candidates.name: Buenos Aires
candidates.summary: A vast, energetic capital where grand architecture, late-night dining, neighborhood cafés and serious cultural life meet a practical big-city rhythm.

candidates.name: Brisbane
candidates.summary: A sunny river city with outdoor living, strong services and fast-growing urban energy, balancing subtropical ease with a practical Australian big-city base.

candidates.name: Bruges
candidates.summary: A compact Flemish heritage city where canals, cycling and medieval streets support an unusually beautiful, walkable everyday lifestyle beyond the tourist core.

candidates.name: Curitiba
candidates.summary: A high-elevation southern Brazilian capital known for parks, organized urban planning and cooler weather, with a practical everyday character beneath its modern image.

candidates.name: Santiago
candidates.summary: A sophisticated Andean capital with strong services, metro connectivity and dramatic mountain views, pairing urban convenience with quick access to wine country and outdoor escapes.

candidates.name: Bogota
candidates.summary: A high-altitude Andean capital with heavyweight culture, food and professional life, offering immense urban variety alongside traffic, weather and neighborhood-selection tradeoffs.

candidates.name: Makarska
candidates.summary: A compact Adriatic town squeezed between clear water and the Biokovo massif, delivering a walkable seaside lifestyle with dramatic scenery and strong seasonal swings.

candidates.name: Aix-en-Provence
candidates.summary: An elegant Provençal university city of fountains, markets and café-lined streets, offering polished daily life with countryside access and excellent regional connections.

candidates.name: Chania
candidates.summary: A Venetian-harbor city in western Crete combining walkable historic streets, excellent food and quick access to beaches, mountains and some of Greece's best outdoor scenery.

candidates.name: Aosta
candidates.summary: A compact Alpine capital surrounded by some of Europe's highest peaks, pairing Roman history and Italian daily life with exceptional access to hiking, skiing and mountain villages.

candidates.name: Kurashiki
candidates.summary: A cultured western Japanese city where the preserved Bikan canal district, museums and textile heritage meet a substantial modern city near the Seto Inland Sea.

candidates.name: Todos Santos
candidates.summary: A small Baja California Sur arts town between desert and Pacific, offering galleries, restaurants and surf-country scenery with a slower rhythm than nearby resort centers.

candidates.name: Muscat
candidates.summary: A low-rise Gulf capital framed by rugged mountains and the Arabian Sea, combining exceptional cleanliness, modern infrastructure and Omani tradition in a car-oriented urban landscape.

candidates.name: Panama City
candidates.summary: A tropical finance and logistics capital with a modern skyline, historic Casco Viejo and easy regional air access, pairing urban convenience with heat, traffic and coastal humidity.

candidates.name: Cape Town
candidates.summary: A spectacular coastal metropolis where Table Mountain, beaches, wine country and serious urban culture create one of the world's strongest city-and-nature combinations.

candidates.name: Seoul
candidates.summary: A hyper-connected global capital where transit, food, shopping and late-night energy operate at extraordinary scale, balanced by mountains, river parks and highly efficient daily systems.

candidates.name: A Coruña
candidates.summary: A compact Galician Atlantic city with beaches inside the urban fabric, a lively waterfront and strong food culture, offering a practical alternative to Spain's larger metros.

candidates.name: Phuket
candidates.summary: Thailand's largest island combines beaches, international services and a mature visitor economy, offering easy tropical living alongside traffic, seasonality and rapid development.

candidates.name: Belfast
candidates.summary: A compact, reinvented Northern Irish capital with strong music, pub and cultural life, improving waterfront districts and easy access to dramatic coast and countryside.

candidates.name: Albuquerque
candidates.summary: A high-desert Southwestern city with dramatic Sandia Mountain access, deep Hispanic and Native cultural influence, spacious living and a distinctive Route 66 identity.
